bullets: S&P futures -1.1%, Nasdaq -2.1% as early Democratic Senate wins raise odds of a Democratic sweep, pressuring risk assets.

AVTR.why: Oct 30 Q3 beat (4th straight) and raised FY guide, but margin headwinds from inflation/mix, Europe weakness and thin 2026 organic growth guide (0.75-1.25%) spooked holders; turnaround seen as already priced in.
AVTR.bull: Fourth consecutive earnings beat and a swing to profit show the turnaround is progressing.
AVTR.bear: Margin headwinds, European weakness and muted 2026 growth guidance show the recovery is still fragile.

MTDR.why: Energy names sold off as crude slid on US-Iran de-escalation hopes. MTDR still beat Q3 EPS by $0.25 (Nov 3) on positive estimate revisions; no company-specific downgrade found in the drop window.
MTDR.bull: Q3 EPS beat by $0.25; the drop tracks an oil-price-driven energy selloff, not a company problem.
MTDR.bear: Further oil weakness from Mideast de-escalation would keep pressuring E&P revenue outlook.

VAL.why: Nov 2 Q3 results: revenue beat ($593.6M vs $573.7M) but EPS missed badly ($0.66 vs $1.13 consensus), driving an ~5-10% post-earnings slide. Analysts hold a $69 target, 23% below spot.
VAL.bull: Revenue beat estimates and stock is still up sharply year-to-date despite the pullback.
VAL.bear: EPS missed consensus by nearly 42%, and analyst price targets imply ~23% further downside.

CRWD.why: Cybersecurity/software extended a sector-wide selloff (AI capex worries after Oracle's $20B raise, Alphabet/Amazon capex) despite a Deutsche Bank upgrade to Buy ($300 PT) and new CoreWeave/Dynatrace/Deloitte partnerships for CRWD.
CRWD.bull: Deutsche Bank just upgraded to Buy with a $300 target; new AI-security partnerships announced despite the dip.
CRWD.bear: Stock is still richly valued after a 120% YTD run, inviting profit-taking on any sector wobble.

CRM.why: Nov 3 decline tied to the $2.7B Cresta acquisition (5th deal this year, undisclosed terms) raising integration/execution concerns, plus a ~609k-share offering for an employee plan adding dilution worries, despite a Q3 EPS beat.
CRM.bull: Q3 EPS beat big ($5.90 vs $3.27 consensus) and revenue grew 10.8% y/y; consensus rating is still Moderate Buy.
CRM.bear: Fifth acquisition this year plus a new share offering raise integration-risk and dilution concerns.

CVLT.why: Oct 27 gap-down was a 'sell the news' reaction to a Q3 beat (EPS $1.38 vs $1.24) with only Hold/Neutral target raises; Nov 2 added sector-wide AI-capex selloff pressure. No clear company damage, but no clean sector story either.
CVLT.bull: Q3 beat on EPS and revenue with ARR up 20%; no analyst downgrades on fundamentals were found.
CVLT.bear: High valuation multiple triggered a 'sell the news' drop even on a beat, and new buy-side support looks limited.

PATH.why: Nov 2 drop tracked a broad software/AI-capex selloff (PATH -2.84% vs S&P -0.51%). The last company-specific hit (DA Davidson/UBS/RBC downgrades on AI-pricing pushback) was Oct 16, outside the recent drop window; no new catalyst found.
PATH.bull: Latest single-day drop simply tracked a broad software selloff; no fresh company-specific news found.
PATH.bear: Elevated 25% short interest and lingering AI-pricing-resistance concerns from mid-October could keep pressuring shares.
